knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A specialty names the client group and the result. A full service list does not tell a prospect whether the service fits them, and price alone is not a specialty.
Explaining the fit and referring on keeps the prospect informed without a refusal based on a protected attribute. Declining by age is the pattern the anti-discrimination point warns about.
Records of clients who stayed and reached their goals show the traits that predict a good match. Guesses and competitor prices do not.

practicalCriteria: Given ten anonymised client records, the learner builds a profile table in which each trait is counted from the records, and the assessor recounts two traits and agrees
The learner writes an ideal-client sentence that names a working pattern or concern from the records and no protected attribute
The learner writes a referral note for one out-of-scope enquiry with a reason tied to the service
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed profile table with record counts
Referral note for one out-of-scope enquiry
stopWorkCriteria: Stop if the learner proposes refusing people on a protected attribute; the assessor redirects before the profile is accepted
Stop if the records include identifying details beyond what the profile needs
